parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in 'up to par'
rot is nonsense or drivel

explanation.surface: Someone churns out the usual nonsense over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words mechanically, like the talking bird.

indicators.note: buried signals letters concealed within the clue's words

explanation.surface: Moving house, someone digs up a hidden hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treasure' suggests a hoard; here it is a beloved person.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind, beloved person is called a treasure or a darling.

clue.text: The guy may be my responsibility

definitions.text: The guy may be my responsibility

parts.words: The guy may be my responsibility
parts.note: a guy is a rope stretched to steady a tent or mast, which a cordage maker would produce

explanation.surface: Someone says they are in charge of a certain man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' reads as a man, but a guy rope is a line holding a tent down.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who twists cordage makes the lines used as guys.

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the shelter goes around the word

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: A shelter stands empty, with nobody inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone renting and living in a property is its occupier.

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: something lost has gone astray, so stray
'eh?' and 'what?' are both requests to repeat something

explanation.surface: Someone has nearly mislaid their hat and asks, puzzled, what was said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims STRAY to STRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater or panama woven from dried stalks is a kind of hat worn in summer.

definitions.meaning: a body of opinion or doctrine held by a group
a faculty (school) devoted to the mind (thought)

explanation.surface: A question about faith residing in the powers of the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' reads as a mental power, but is also a university department.
explanation.definitionFit: A shared doctrine is a school of opinion; read literally, it is a teaching department of the mind.

indicators.note: gone in the sense of gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
finally picks out the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Mum has at last moved into a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' rearranges MOTHERS plus E, the last letter of 'here'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly mother might finally move into a residential care home.

definitions.meaning: a thin slice, as of biscuit or silicon
microchips are made on a thin disc of silicon

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: cut, and serve fries on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' suggests fried potatoes; they are silicon microchips.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin disc of silicon carries microchips, and a thin slice is also so called.

clue.text: Star playing in a real band

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about freely

explanation.surface: A celebrity performs with a proper group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity musician; it is a heavenly body.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright red giant in Taurus, the bull's eye, is a named star.

clue.text: Plant pot like this on cooker

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece 'on' another is placed after it

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of range cooker
a pan is a cooking pot
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: Instructions for setting a pot on the stove just so.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a heavy cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: The African lily, with its globes of blue flowers, is a garden flowering species.

parts.note: a craze is a passing fad

explanation.surface: A passing trend connected with the 1990s boy band East 17.
explanation.walkthrough: The '17' that seems to belong to the band name is the definition, pointing to the answer at 17-down. East 17 was a British pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: In film, one shot dissolving into another is a gradual fading transition; things that melt away also fade.

parts.note: an old flame is a former partner or lover
NCO is a non-commissioned officer, a soldier

explanation.surface: A list pairing a dancing partner with a soldier, as at a regimental ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish gypsy style of dancing, with stamping feet and castanets.

clue.text: Pick up purchase, talking through this?

indicators.note: talking signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, and a purchase is a buy

explanation.surface: A query about collecting something bought, perhaps on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word meaning by means of this, as in a legal declaration.

parts.note: a gambler succeeds with a win
K stands for a thousand, as in 'a salary of 30K'

explanation.surface: A punter lands a grand on a little bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' looks like a small bet, matching the gambling surface; it is the definition, a quick blink of an eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluttering an eyelid quickly is a brief blink of the eye.

clue.text: On edge, I completely upset kid

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: all means completely, as in 'all alone'
to kid is to tease

explanation.surface: A nervous person confesses to upsetting a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling nervous and uncomfortable is being on edge.

clue.text: I mean it when I say …

definitions.meaning: a promise that one is speaking sincerely
a signal to act on a spoken command, as in 'go on my command'

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are serious, then trails off before giving the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an oath of sincerity and the cue to start at someone's signal.

parts.note: with can mean given, as in 'with luck'
a stand is a support

explanation.surface: Once backed up, someone takes on a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist an attack is to fight it off.

clue.text: Rising deficit central to club's collapse

indicators.note: being central to a word puts a piece in its middle

parts.note: a dive is a seedy nightclub

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: Mounting debts lie behind a club's demise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns LOSS into SSOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To break up or fall apart, as a parliament or marriage is ended.

clue.text: Weapon carried by very famous scaremonger

indicators.note: something carried by another is held inside it

parts.note: A-list describes the most famous celebrities
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A celebrity armed with a weapon spreads panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises needless panic is a scaremonger, spreading fear.

clue.text: Look after the dying in Yorkshire?

indicators.note: Yorkshire dialect clips the word 'the' to a bare t', so its last two letters drop

parts.note: the dying of something is its end, so 'the end'

explanation.surface: A question about caring for people at the end of life in a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously shortens 'the' to t', so 'the end' becomes t'end.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend a patient or a garden is to care for it.

clue.text: About to leave, ticks off register

indicators.note: a piece set to leave is removed from the word

parts.note: to tick off is to reprimand, or censure
re means about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A person about to depart crosses names off a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticks off' suggests marking a list; it means scolds.
explanation.definitionFit: An official count of the population is a register of residents.

clue.text: Can supply device to restrain offender

definitions.meaning: a shop that has goods available to sell keeps them in its inventory
an old wooden frame locking the ankles of a wrongdoer in public

explanation.surface: A shop boasts it can provide a restraint for criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop that carries goods can supply them; the old punishment frame held feet in holes.

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece holding up another sits beneath it

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier lifts his pet pooch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation like 'My!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The short-legged Welsh breed favoured by the late Queen is a type of dog.

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, so the letter O
verse is poetry
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Romantic poems written while travelling in foreign parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in or to a foreign country.

clue.text: Behind circling duck, another one in the air

indicators.note: circling means going around another piece

parts.note: aft means behind, at the stern of a ship
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
a second duck, again O

explanation.surface: A pair of birds fly overhead, one tailing another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the air' looks literal; it means happening or brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going on or brewing is said to be underway.

indicators.note: one thing bathed in another is surrounded by it

parts.note: far means distant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lone figure glows in faraway light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like illumination; here it means pale in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair or skin is pale or light in colour.

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: corrupt means these letters are distorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest Member of Parliament stands trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges TRIALSO into ISLATOR. In cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament makes laws, so is a lawmaker.

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it

parts.note: the occupant at 4-down pays rent to the landlord
a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: An occupant, or the occupant's rent money, used to fund a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Both '4's point to 4-down, an occupant who pays rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in a property, such as a flat's occupier, is one who lives there.

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to date them

explanation.surface: A burial ground is found deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' wants to be the burial place of the surface; it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and sedate both describe a calm, serious, dignified manner.
